doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: European recordings and return to America
title: Returning to America to teach at New England Conservatory
summary: Gunther Schuller, then president, invited him to the Conservatory in 1969; Russell was no longer married.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: That was another opportunity. Again at the end of the ’60s, you were – we find you returning to the United States. As I understand it, Gunther Schuller contacted you.
Yeah, he did.
There was a newly formed jazz department at the New England Conservatory of Music?
Yeah, that was 1949, I think.
’49. 1969? No, no. It had to be 1949.
That’s the summer. You all talked about it yesterday, the summer workshop that you did.
Wait a minute.
Gunther Schuller was head of the classical there, but not the jazz.
I could be wrong, but . . .
You’re probably thinking about a different association with Gunther. But I mean when you came to the New England Conservatory of Music to begin teaching. That was ’69, I believe.
’69, yeah.
Was Gunther the president of the Conservatory at the time?
Sure was.
So – the department had just been formed? Is that my understanding?
Um-hmm.

So that must have been exciting. It kind of meant that you were coming in on the ground floor for a new part of the organization. The organization was pretty old, but there was a new part of it that they were bringing in, and you were coming in at the same time? Is that correct?
I guess you’re right. I’m not clear on whether they had a jazz program before I was there, but there was a jazz program after.

One of – I’ve heard from several different sources, and I’ve read also as well, that it was newly formed. I’ve never seen any specific dates, but it was newly formed, and Gunther Schuller wanted you to be a part of it. Of course you and he had an association that went back 20 years before that, at least.
I met Gunther at John Lewis’s 20 years before that. Our association wasn’t proven until ’69. He did send a telegram. It was my time to return to America.
Were you still married at this point, when you returned to America?
No. No, I wasn’t.

So your return to the scene was as a – you were turning in your expatriate card, coming back as s single musician who had just had a fantastic experience and had been guest conductor of Finnish national radio, Danish national radio, Norwegian national radio, Swedish national radio, Italian and German national radio.
